description: Calendar date of the inventory/sales observation, stored as a full timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format (all times are 00:00:00 because observations are daily, not intra-day). Covers the full calendar year 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31 (366 days). Sourced from the original file or synthetically generated to fill coverage gaps.

Unique product identifier in the format SKU followed by a zero-padded 4-digit number (SKU0001 to SKU0500). Represents one of 500 distinct stock-keeping units. This column is product-constant: every row for the same product carries the same product_id.

Product category. One of four values: Grocery (approx. 35% of products), Electronics (approx. 20%), HomeDecor (approx. 20%), Apparel (approx. 25%). Assigned once per product using the mode of source records or synthetic assignment; product-constant after normalisation.

Calendar season label for the observation date, derived from the month: Winter = December/January/February; Summer = March/April/May/June; Monsoon = July/August/September; Festive = October/November. Used as a categorical feature in demand-forecasting models.

Quantity of the product in stock (units) at the time of the observation. Non-negative integer. Represents a point-in-time snapshot; the latest record per product is used as the current inventory estimate. Values can reach zero (stockout recorded). Not a running balance – each row is an independent observation.

Fixed replenishment trigger threshold for the product (units). When stock_qty falls to or below this level, a reorder is recommended. Computed as the median of source values per product, or synthetically assigned (range 20–100 units) for products absent from the original file. Product-constant after normalisation.

Recorded or synthetically generated daily sales volume for the product on the observation date (units sold). Non-negative integer. Used as the target variable in ML demand-forecasting models and as the input to the mean-demand proxy for reorder calculations. Synthetic values include illustrative seasonal multipliers: +20% in April-June (summer), +40% in the Diwali window (Oct 20 - Nov 5), +8% on weekends.

Unit procurement cost of the product, assumed to be in Indian Rupees (INR). Ranges vary by category: Grocery INR 20–900, Electronics INR 500–25000, HomeDecor INR 100–8000, Apparel INR 150–5000. Computed as the median of source values per product or synthetically drawn from the category range. Product-constant after normalisation. Sensitive: the Anonymise Pricing toggle in the dashboard hides raw values.

Identifier of the product's supplier, in the format SUP followed by a zero-padded 2-digit number (SUP01 to SUP30). Assigned as the mode of source records per product or randomly from the 30 supplier pool for synthetic products. Product-constant after normalisation. Used in the Suppliers tab to aggregate spend, lead times, and stock risk per supplier.

Supplier lead time: the number of calendar days from placing a replenishment order to receiving stock. Non-negative integer, range 3–21 days. Computed as the median of source values per product or synthetically drawn (3–21 days) for missing products. Product-constant after normalisation. Used in the target-stock formula: target_stock = estimated_daily_demand * lead_days * (1 + safety_pct/100).
